questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, you need to:
questions.explanation: When your motorcycle speeds up, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A yellow traffic light warns you that the signal will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: To avoid getting tired on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Limit how much you ride each day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Limit how much you ride each day.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest, even if you don't feel tired. Most experienced riders limit themselves to six hours of riding per day. Wind, cold, and rain make you tire faster, so dress to protect yourself from the weather.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Drift into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause you to drift into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: Which material gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather and sturdy synthetic materials provide the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright, reflective clothing whenever you ride, no matter the time.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Should be checked often by riders.
Don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked often by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make this head check a habit.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible to other drivers. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: Which of these is not recommended protective gear for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Wear protective gear when riding. Good protection includes long-sleeved jackets, heavy long pants, closed-toe boots that cover your ankles, and full-fingered leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible.

questions.question: To get the most protection from your helmet, make sure it:
questions.explanation: Your helmet protects you best when it meets DOT and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Not make sudden movements, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not make sudden movements, if possible.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Speed up, shift gears, turn, and brake smoothly.

questions.question: Riding in the left third of the lane lets the driver see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind may block the side mirror.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane where the driver is more likely to see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: To lower your risk of a collision, you should:

options.text: Never swerve to avoid a hazard.
Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds to spot hazards early. This gives you time to react before you reach the danger.

questions.question: If you must ride on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently.

questions.question: To be seen more easily by other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you at any time of day.

questions.question: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to:
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Most U.S. motorcycles made after 1978 turn on the headlight automatically when running. Check that your headlight works before every ride.

questions.question: Wind noise:

options.text: Is easy to get used to.

questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise exposure can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear plugs or other hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Unlike other beverages, alcohol:

options.text: Is absorbed into the bloodstream right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is absorbed into the bloodstream right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It is absorbed directly through the stomach and small intestine walls, enters the bloodstream quickly, and reaches the brain fast.

questions.question: Which material gives the best protection in a crash?
questions.explanation: Leather or synthetic materials protect riders best in an accident. Always wear long pants and a jacket when riding.

questions.question: Riding directly alongside another vehicle is:

options.text: Safe because you are in a separate lane.
Recommended because it blocks the wind.
Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside other vehicles. The driver may not see you in their blind spot and could move into your lane.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
Should not be a concern, since the motorcycle has two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Using proper braking technique is essential for safe riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic ahead will be merging.

questions.question: When scanning around your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Look for possible escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
See if you can travel faster than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for possible escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
questions.explanation: While looking for hazards, focus on finding escape routes at intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones.
